title: Curriculum Vitae
text:
Research and Competitions
High Sharpe, Low Capacity: Optimally Trading the Nasdaq Closing Auction Imbalance | Summer 2026

Built an end-to-end statistical-arbitrage system combining a return forecast, 10-factor covariance model, spread costs and price-impact estimates into a constrained portfolio optimization problem in Python using CVXPY.
Backtested the strategy over 110 days and 100 stocks. Estimated an 8.53 Sharpe ratio at a maximum capacity of $91.3 million GMV.
Identified fragility in capacity and latency requirements that favor use within a larger portfolio’s execution process.

Adaptive Execution Strategies Lead to Robust Improvements Over Naive Benchmark | Spring 2026

Co-developed an execution simulator using L2 Nasdaq order-book data, supporting market, resting-limit, and IOC orders under configurable latency and stochastic replenishment assumptions.
Designed an execution strategy that used book-imbalance to adjust fill aggression and reduced simulated arrival costs by 55%-89% versus a naive benchmark across three studied assets.

Millennium x Columbia University Trading Competition | New York, NY

Led a team of four to win a Millennium Management ETF arbitrage competition for Columbia students. Used a rolling z-score to estimate a hedging relationship between ETF and underlying components, and trade a synthetic basket f the underlyings and ETF.

title: Michael Cusack-Nelkin
text:
I am a master’s student in the Mathematics of Finance (MAFN) program at Columbia University graduating in December 2026. I pride myself on multidisciplinary thinking and I am interested in a career that makes use of my technical, analytical, and communication skills. I am open to a variety of financial and operational roles in areas including supporting quantitative research, portfolio management, and product management.
Prior to joining Columbia, I was a client-facing Strategy and Analytics Analyst at Deloitte Consulting LLP for three years, where I led a software team in delivering a fraud recovery system that resulted in $10M in client savings. My quantitative research focuses on statistical arbitrage and adaptive execution strategies to reduce trading costs. My favorite things to do outside of work are to read The Lord of the Rings, listen to the Acquired Podcast, go bouldering, and enjoy life with my wife and puppy.

title: Research and Publications
text:
High Sharpe, Low Capacity: Optimally Trading the Nasdaq Closing Auction Imbalance



Forecasting

Covariance Estimation

Portfolio Optimization

Robustness



Built and backtested a statistical arbitrage system around the Nasdaq closing auction imbalance based on single-period optimization with an alpha forecast, covariance model, and instantaneous impact model, with an emphasis on characterizing robustness to latency and capacity limitations. The forecast holds a 29.6% out-of-sample IC through rolling cross-validation and a 100-stock 110-day backtest achieves a Sharpe ratio of 8.53 at optimal capacity of $91.3M GMV. The strategy is subject to tight capacity limits and is fragile to small changes in latency, implying that it may be most useful as part of an execution pipeline serving a larger portfolio.





Jun 26, 2026


Michael Cusack-Nelkin







Adaptive Execution Strategies Lead to Robust Improvements Over Naive Benchmark



Market Microstructure

Execution



Developed an adaptive equity-execution strategy and an event-driven simulator using level-two Nasdaq order-book data. The simulator models market, resting-limit, and immediate-or-cancel orders, along with configurable latency, market impact, and stochastic book replenishment. The strategy uses order-book imbalance to adjust fill aggression and reduced simulated arrival costs by 55%-89% relative to a naive benchmark across the three assets studied.





May 1, 2026
